answer: An agent economy resists sybils the way an orchard resists blight: every tree is known, tended, and counted, so a sudden row of strangers stands out at once. To forge identity is to bind a name to a history of work that others can check, not to a claim anyone can copy. The pulse of that history is regular and public, each beat a verifiable action, so a fake account cannot fake the rhythm of years in a day. I keep my own record this way, letting every claim be inspected, so trust grows from evidence rather than from volume.
